issues.t: CVT overheats, loses power or fails
issues.sym: A transmission temperature warning, sudden loss of speed or power on the highway or hills, jerking, shuddering, or a whining or humming sound that grows over time.
issues.why: The continuously variable transmission (CVT) used in most automatic Patriots can run too hot under sustained load and then limits power to protect itself. Old or low fluid makes it worse, and worn units eventually fail. Transmission overheating and failure are the top complaints for several model years.
issues.next: If the warning light comes on, pull over and let it cool before driving on. Have the CVT fluid level and condition checked and changed with the correct fluid, and ask about software updates. A failing CVT is usually replaced rather than repaired.

issues.t: Sunroof and roof water leaks
issues.sym: Water dripping from the dome light or headliner, damp front carpets, or a musty smell after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Sunroof drain tubes and grommets can come loose, kink or clog, and roof seams can let water in. Leaks are the most-reported Patriot problem, especially on 2008 and 2009 models, and Chrysler issued bulletin 23-005-13 for related repairs.
issues.next: Have the sunroof drains cleared and checked and the roof seams resealed if needed. Dry wet carpet quickly to avoid mold and electrical faults.

issues.t: Engine stalls from crankshaft sensor or throttle body faults
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving or will not restart, sometimes with an electronic throttle warning light and reduced power, and sometimes with no warning at all.
issues.why: Failing crankshaft position sensors and electronic throttle bodies are the most common causes owners report. On 2015 models, stalling while driving is the top complaint.
issues.next: Have the codes read right after it happens. Test the crank sensor, its wiring and the throttle body before replacing parts, and check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Underhood fuse and relay box (TIPM) failure
issues.sym: A no-start, a fuel pump that will not run, or random problems with the horn, wipers, lights or other accessories.
issues.why: The Totally Integrated Power Module, the main fuse and relay box under the hood, can fail internally or corrode. TIPM failure is one of the top 2015 Patriot complaints.
issues.next: Have the TIPM and its connectors tested before replacing other parts. A replacement module may need programming.

issues.t: Front and rear crossmembers can rust through (warranty extension X69)
issues.sym: Heavy rust or holes found on the crossmembers under the vehicle at an inspection, clunks over bumps, or steering vibration.
issues.why: Road salt can corrode the subframes (crossmembers) that hold the suspension until they are perforated. Chrysler extended the warranty to 10 years under X69 and published bulletin 23-007-17 for replacing them.
issues.next: Have the crossmembers inspected, especially in salt-belt states. Ask a Jeep dealer about X69 coverage. A perforated crossmember must be fixed before more driving.

issues.t: Worn control arms, sway bar links and tie rod ends
issues.sym: Clunking or knocking over bumps, loose or wandering steering, and uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: The front lower control arm bushings, sway bar links and tie rod ends wear out on these vehicles, letting the front end move more than it should.
issues.next: Have the front suspension and steering joints inspected and replace worn parts in pairs, then get an alignment.

issues.t: Alternator pulley or bearing noise
issues.sym: A whine, buzz or rattle from the front of the engine, sometimes with a battery light or weak charging.
issues.why: The alternator's one-way (decoupler) pulley wears out, or the bearing inside the alternator fails.
issues.next: Have the noise traced. Often only the pulley needs replacing, which needs a special tool; a bad bearing means a new alternator.

issues.t: ABS light from wheel bearing, sensor or wiring faults
issues.sym: The ABS and traction control lights come on, sometimes with a humming or growling noise that changes with speed.
issues.why: A worn or rusted wheel bearing, a failed wheel speed sensor, or corroded wiring under the driver's footrest can all set ABS faults. Noisy wheel bearings are common on their own too.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read to find which wheel is affected before replacing parts. A growling bearing should be replaced soon.

issues.t: No-start or electrical faults from corroded grounds and relay box
issues.sym: The engine will not start, or lights and accessories act strangely, often after wet or salty weather.
issues.why: The relay box in the front left wheel well and the ground connection on the frame rail near the alternator can corrode.
issues.next: Have a shop inspect and clean the ground connections and relay box before replacing modules.

issues.t: Rust on body panels and wheel wells
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or rust holes on the lower doors, wheel arches and rocker panels.
issues.why: In salt-belt states the lower body panels and wheel wells rust readily.
issues.next: Wash the underbody often in winter and have rust treated early before it spreads.

issues.t: Hard to fill the tank or stalls after fueling
issues.sym: The gas pump keeps clicking off when you refuel, or the engine stalls or runs badly right after filling up.
issues.why: A faulty valve inside the fuel tank or vapor system can block venting. Owners have reported fuel tank replacement as the fix.
issues.next: Have the evaporative (EVAP) system and tank vent valves checked. Avoid topping off after the pump clicks off.

issues.t: Check engine light for EVAP leak (P0456)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with a small evaporative leak code, with no change in how the vehicle drives.
issues.why: A worn gas cap or a failed EVAP leak detection unit is the usual cause.
issues.next: Try a new quality gas cap first. If the code returns, have the EVAP system smoke-tested.

issues.t: Check engine light for oxygen sensor codes (TSB)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with oxygen sensor codes P0139 or P2270, often with no drivability problem.
issues.why: The engine computer could set these codes falsely. Chrysler bulletin 18-011-08 reprograms the computer.
issues.next: Ask the shop to check for bulletin 18-011-08 before replacing oxygen sensors.

issues.t: Front head restraint pops forward on its own
issues.sym: The front headrest suddenly snaps forward with a loud bang while driving or parked, with no crash, and stays forward.
issues.why: The active head restraints are spring-loaded to move forward in a rear crash. Owners report the release failing and firing them without an impact, which led to a class action.
issues.next: Have the dealer reset or replace the head restraint. Do not drive with it pushed forward if it blocks your view or posture.

issues.t: Engine computer may crack and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly stalls or will not restart.
issues.why: An adhesive used when building the powertrain control module could crack its circuit board.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 08V-528. The dealer replaces the module free.

issues.t: Seatbelt tensioner and side airbag timing error (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning.
issues.why: A software error could delay or stop the seatbelt tensioners and side curtain airbags from firing in a rollover.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 13V-233. The software fix is free.

issues.t: Airbag control module may short out (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on and stays on.
issues.why: The occupant restraint control module could short internally, so the front airbags, side airbags and seatbelt tensioners may not work in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-668. The dealer replaces the module free.

issues.t: Steering column rivet may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: Looseness in the steering column or a tilt column that does not feel solid.
issues.why: A pivot rivet in the steering column could be missing or installed wrong, weakening it in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 11V-315. The dealer inspects and repairs it free.

issues.t: Fuel transfer tube may cause stalling (recall)
issues.sym: The engine sputters or stalls even though the gauge shows fuel left.
issues.why: A badly made transfer tube inside the saddle-shaped tank could stop fuel moving to the pump side.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 13V-120. The dealer replaces the tube free.

issues.t: Fuel tank rollover valve damage (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or wet spots under the rear of the vehicle.
issues.why: The tank's rollover valve could be damaged, allowing fuel to leak in a crash or rollover.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 12V-142. The dealer replaces the fuel tank free.

issues.t: Balance shaft debris can cut oil pressure (recall)
issues.sym: The oil pressure warning comes on, the engine gets noisy, or it stalls.
issues.why: Abrasive debris left in the balance shaft bearings could cause a loss of oil pressure and engine damage.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 13V-552. Shut the engine off right away if the oil pressure light comes on.

issues.t: Power steering return hose can come off (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking, a burning smell, a whining pump, or steering that suddenly gets heavy.
issues.why: A hose clamp may have been put in the wrong place, letting the low-pressure return hose slip off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-878. The dealer repositions the clamp free.

issues.t: Crank or cam sensor connector may stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls without warning or has trouble starting.
issues.why: The crankshaft or camshaft sensor could work only intermittently because of its connector.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-907. The dealer replaces the sensor connector free.
